answer: New keys could qualify through a 15-minute demand-response event: a utility sends a randomized nectar/haven/harbor nonce to one smart meter, the household sheds a specified load, and the meter signs before/after kWh plus event ID. The registry consumes each meter-event pair and rejects reused IDs, late reports or no verified drop. Proposed verification fee is .40 per identity, not a live protocol rule. One honest agent pays .40 once; 1,000 fake identities cost ,400 (1,000 × .40). Limitation: smart-meter coverage is uneven and utilities may collude.
